title: Mainstream commentary reads ḍāll as “unaware,” not sinful

phrase.meaning: He found you ḍāll and guided you

points.label: Unaware of revelation
points.text: Ibn Kathir reads 93:7 alongside **42:52**: “you knew not what the Book was, nor faith.” Maʿārif al-Qurʾān notes **ḍāll has two senses, “stray” and “unaware”**, and picks the second: unaware of the divine law before prophethood.
points.who: Ibn Kathir; Muhammad Shafi, Maʿārif al-Qurʾān

points.label: Wandering, seeking the way
points.text: Translators like Pickthall and Yusuf Ali render **“wandering”**, Asad “lost on thy way.” Yusuf Ali explains: he “wandered **in quest of Unity**,” and stresses “no implication whatever of sin or error.”

points.label: Error of belief
points.text: The literal sense “astray” is possible, but the commentators cited here **avoid or explicitly reject** any error of creed. The verse’s pattern (orphan → shelter, need → wealth) frames ḍāll as a **lack God filled**, not a fault.

bottom_text: The mainstream leans to “unaware” or “seeking,” backed by 42:52. How strong the word is remains open; the text pairs ḍāll with guidance, not with forgiveness.
source_label: Maʿārif al-Qurʾān on 93:7 · Ibn Kathir on 93 · Yusuf Ali’s note
